## Natural history notes

A tiny pygmy grasshopper characterized by its short compact body, rough-textured pronotum extending over the abdomen, strong hind legs, and dark side markings that give it the “black-sided” appearance. In Florida, the Black-sided Pygmy Grasshopper is found in moist open habitats such as pond edges, marsh margins, wet ditches, muddy trails, stream banks, and low grassy wetlands where bare soil, algae, and short vegetation occur. It feeds mainly on algae, mosses, detritus, and fine plant material at the soil surface, moving with quick hops through damp ground-layer microhabitats and serving as prey for frogs, spiders, birds, and predatory insects.
